I have used Microsoft products from pretty much the start. The first "OS" i used was Microsoft MSX Basic, then i updated to DOS learning pretty much all that was there to learn, then they forced me to switch to Windows 95 (i loved DOS and i still think that it was a mistake to leave it), then 98, then 2K, then XP...

Around Win2k i also tried Linux. At first it only lasted one month or so in dual boot... then one day, for apparently no reason, i lost a big chunk of my data. That gave me the motivation to just drop Windows and move to Linux and stick to it (for i think 10 years or so).

Linux is great, the thing that i like the most is that the graphical interface is optional and that you can access to the textual console from the GUI, stand alone, via serial port, via modem, via SSH, etc. and, from there, you can pretty much do anything you like. Also, by default, it installs lots of very useful tools (especially command line tools), while Windows comes almost empty and you have to install them by yourself.

Also i liked how much and deeply you can customize it. You can pretty much see all its internals and you can change it if you like (and if you know how to do it and have free time).

Lately though i am switching back to Windows. First with Windows 7 then Windows 10. Some things are just easier and quite frankly i was tired of fiddling with hardware and software that wouldn't just work. Sometimes i would try to compile something and it complained because i didn't have that library installed or that version of the kernel or the libraries i had were too old... and if i tried to manually install new libraries this would break preinstalled softwares.

While the open source community is great it is mostly composed by people that dedicates their free time to their projects... which is great, but this sometimes makes development slow and several professional software just can't adopt this philosophy... leaving you without tools that you might want to use or with tools that just aren't so good.

I do not like messing with my OS too much and i don't like reinstalls because then i am forced to re-costumize my system as i like/need (and trust me, i customize it deeply) and by becoming older i don't enjoy anymore so much wasting time on these details... i have other interests (too) now and i would like to use my time in different ways.

I also found that some complex things are apparently simpler with Windows than with Linux... for instance, on Windows, with gpedit, i can easily enable or disable the automatic installation of new devices, while keeping the older ones working. That means that if i plug a recognized device Windows will just use it, but if i try to install a new devices (such as an unknown usb-stick, or an external Firewire port) it will just say that the Admin disabled it. This is useful for instance if you don't want your friends (or random attackers) to plug random hardware in your PC but you still want to use your USB-sticks and your own hardware. While it is true that you cannot see the source code of Windows it is also true that it is very much customizable if you really want to and there is a lot of documentation online about how to do it.

I don't really like the new anti-privacy moves of Microsoft, but i acknowledge that they are not anymore the assholes they used to be. They are releasing tons of interesting stuff as opensource and they seem more motivated to support Linux and other platforms now that Ballmer went away.

Sooo i don't know... I have mixed feelings... i still like and use Linux, but i feel at home in Windows too.
